subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` impose a new unconditional 1 MiB maximum, or should it retain support for larger existing body files while using a different resource-safe strategy?
rationale: This is a public CLI behavior change for existing inputs, and the repository policy treats new limits and removed fallbacks as compatibility-sensitive rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve existing large-file behavior
options.body: Use a streaming or explicitly bounded implementation whose limit is derived from an established downstream contract, without adding a new 1 MiB rejection for existing users.

options.title: Approve and document the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Keep the hard cap only if the memory-wiki owner explicitly accepts the upgrade break and requires documentation, migration or recovery guidance, and focused compatibility proof.

options.title: Pause this PR
options.body: Close or defer the change until a supported size policy and user-facing rationale are agreed.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing large-file behavior
recommendation.body: Use a streaming or explicitly bounded implementation whose limit is derived from an established downstream contract, without adding a new 1 MiB rejection for existing users.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline explicitly routes review attention to this person, though code-history ownership could not be independently confirmed.
